title: Micro-rollout heuristics and telemetry notes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a lightweight, micro-canary rollout pattern we want to try for low-risk model variant changes (quantization, small op fusion kernel swap, tiny weight diff). Focus: observable safety checks, fast aborts, and an explicit pin/unpin flow for customer-facing routes.

Context & constraints:
- Target env: dedicated + hosted (stretch goal: private).
- Traffic shape: steady 200 QPS on endpoint /generate, median request length ~120 tokens, 95th around 800 tokens.
- We want short-lived micro-canaries (minutes -> hours) to validate no regressions in latency or quality before increasing traffic.
- Prefer automated gating over manual eyeballing.

TL;DR proposal:
- Start with 0.5% traffic -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% (or pin at any step). Each step duration: 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, then final bake 6h.
- Hard abort conditions evaluated at 1m cadence, with pre-flight baseline and rolling-window comparison.
- Metrics used: p50/p95 latency, request error rate (5xx + model-runtime errors), token-per-second throughput, user-visible quality signals (rerank score delta, hallucination rate proxy), cost-per-token delta.

Micro-canary phases (concrete):
- Phase 0: Preflight smoke on staging with synthetic low-latency, edge QA signoff. Run smoke-suite (see list below).
- Phase 1 (0.5% traffic, 10m): monitor with immediate abort rules. Manual owner on-call notified if any soft threshold crossed.
- Phase 2 (2% traffic, 15m): raise confidence; look for trend continuity.
- Phase 3 (10% traffic, 30m): deeper quality checks (prompt set eval running in parallel).
- Phase 4 (30% traffic, 1h): scale test to surface concurrency/queueing problems.
- Phase 5 (100% or pin): final rollout; bake for 6h with relaxed but ongoing checks.

Alerting / Abort rules (hard):
- Latency p95 increased > 40% relative to baseline over a 5m window -> abort.
- Error rate (5xx + runtime errors) > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline -> abort.
- Token-per-second throughput drop > 30% (indicative of CPU stalls) -> abort.
- Quality signal: automated eval on canonical prompt set shows > 5% regression in pass-rate OR mean rerank-score drops by > 0.15 -> abort.
- Cost-per-token increases > 20% without latency improvement -> abort (flag finance).

Soft signals (not immediate abort, but require human review):
- Increased variance in p50 (burstiness) -> paging to eng-sre for investigation.
- Latency p95 increase between 20-40% -> slowed progression and extended observation window.

Gating implementation notes (how this will be evaluated):
- Use our rollout controller to route traffic percentage. Controller emits events every minute with current split and candidate metrics snapshot.
- Baseline: last 48h rolling median for metrics, excluding known incidents.
- Compare candidate vs baseline using a small sample-corrected z-test (or bootstrap) to avoid noise-driven aborts.
- Keep a retention buffer of raw traces for 24h for postmortem (span + response payload hashes).

Quality checks / smoke-suite (run on every phase start):
- quick-smoke.sh: health endpoints (+/metrics), model warms, KV cache priming
- prompt-smoke.json: 25 representative prompts (short, long, edge) -> check token counts, stop sequences, basic hallucination heuristics
- integration-check: call downstream client adapters (e.g., our JS/Go SDK) to ensure streaming and function-calling remained stable

Pinning & config notes:
- Pin via rollout config: rollout.spec.pin_version = "v2025-03-12-kq8" (immutable id). Add comment with GH PR/commit.
- Unpin: set pin_version = null and trigger canary with the new variant.
- For immediate reversion, use controller command: redwoodctl rollout set-split --route /generate --variant baseline --percent 100 --reason "abort: latency spike". This should be idempotent and fast (<5s to enact).

Telemetry queries (examples to copy):
- p95 latency (PromQL):
  quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)))
- error rate: sum(rate(requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
- hallucination proxy: sum(rate(hallucination_flag_count[5m])) / sum(rate(completions_total[5m]))

Runbook for owner when alerts fire:
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty, set status in rollout-controller to PAUSED.
2) Quickly check traces for tail latency vs queue size; link to the last 100 traces.
3) If immediate revert is safe, execute redwoodctl command to switch to baseline and annotate incident.
4) If not revert-safe, reduce traffic to 0.1% and page SRE + model-ops.
5) Capture debug logs and save to /tmp/rollout-debug-<timestamp>.tar.gz, add to JIRA REL-1123.

Data collection & experiment hygiene:
- Tag all canary requests with header X-Canary: micro-ep-2025-03.
- Save sample outputs (1 in 100 requests) to dedicated S3 prefix for manual inspection.
- Always run the canonical prompt-set eval in parallel (asynchronous) to compute pass-rate and delta. If eval job fails, treat as a soft-fail and extend observation.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How noisy are rerank-score deltas across prompt-set? Need baseline variance per-prompt.
- Decide who has final "override" authority to push through a canary that fails soft checks (product? eng lead?). Add to runbook.
- Automate the smoke-suite to run as a preflight gating check in CI -> maybe a special job in release pipeline.
- Confirm redwoodctl permissions for on-call rotation, prepare short cheat-sheet for on-call.

Post-rollout follow-up (if successful):
- Schedule a 1-hour retro in #eng-release within 48h. Attach sample traces and eval summaries.
- Update the release notes with pin id, baseline commit, and observed deltas (latency/cost/quality).

Quick snippets (cheat-sheet):
- Pin command example: redwoodctl rollout pin --route /generate --variant v2025-03-12-kq8 --reason "QA approved"
- Revert: redwoodctl rollout set-split --route /generate --variant baseline --percent 100 --reason "auto-abort"
- Audit: redwoodctl rollout history --route /generate --since 24h

Notes to self (end):
Keep this lightweight. The goal is fast validation with clear aborts and minimal blast radius. Revisit thresholds after first three micro-rollouts and tune using observed false-positive rate.

-- Evan
